subject: Week 18: finalize the allergen-introduction plan before solids

content.hook: Solids are about eight weeks out, and the allergen-introduction plan is the decision to settle first: Avi's eczema and family-history risk tier determines whether peanut starts at home around 6 months or under an allergist's supervision at 4-6 months.
content.thisWeek: Days 124-130 sit mid-stretch between the 4-month vaccines and the 6-month milestones: brief tripod sitting, one-handed reaching, and consonant babble (ba, da, ga) with vocal turn-taking are the headline developments. Rolling both directions is emerging for some - the CDC checkpoint for rolling tummy-to-back is 6 months, so its absence now is not a flag. Socially he distinguishes you from strangers and anticipates being picked up.
watchFors: [low concern] Teething signs - drool, gum-rubbing, chewing everything, extra fussiness. Symptoms front-run the first tooth by weeks; eruption typically waits until 6-10 months.
[monitor] Night sleep not consolidating 4-6 weeks past regression onset despite a stable routine and environment - log the wakings and bring the log to the 6-month visit.
[call within 24h] Persistent or worsening eczema - it moves him into a higher allergen-introduction risk tier, and that conversation must happen before peanut does.
[call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher, fewer than five wet diapers in 24 hours, labored breathing, or blue lips or unresponsiveness - 911 for breathing or color change.

enrichment.body: Finalize the allergen plan by risk tier: severe eczema or known egg allergy means a pediatric allergist before peanut; mild eczema or family history means a pediatrician conversation about a 4-6-month start per the LEAP-derived guidelines; no risk factors means peanut arrives around 6 months with other solids.
Protect open floor time - rolling practice is organic now, with him flipping in and out of tummy time on his own. Keep container time (seats, swings) to a minimum during wake windows.

Anchor the post-regression bedtime routine: bath, feed, book, song - same order nightly, drowsy-but-awake into the crib, bedtime in the 18:00-19:00 slot. Most infants consolidate within 2-6 weeks of a consistent response strategy.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep

subject: Week 19: choking-hazard audit - everything goes in the mouth now

content.hook: Deliberate mouthing arrives this week - every object he can grab goes straight in. That is exactly how he should be exploring, which makes the floor-level choking-hazard audit this weekend's job.
content.thisWeek: Days 131-137 are the pre-solids consolidation week: tripod sitting with hands forward for 5-10 seconds, deliberate bring-to-mouth exploration of texture, babble strings with real intonation, and laughing at peek-a-boo. Rolling is possible or emerging - the CDC 2022 checkpoint is 6 months, so no rolling yet is within range. A few early movers rock on hands and knees; more typically that lands at 6-10 months.
watchFors: [low concern] Everything in the mouth - necessary developmental exploration, not a behavior to discourage. Supervise and control the floor instead.
[low concern] 30-45-minute catnaps - common at this age and typically lengthening by 5-6 months. If he wakes content and the next wake window holds, the nap is doing its job.
[monitor] Persistent inability to bear weight on his legs when held standing, or no rolling in either direction - worth a line in the 6-month visit notes.
[call within 24h] Fever of 100.4F rectal or higher with reduced feeding, or acute illness onset with unusual irritability - same-day call.
[call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher, sudden-onset lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

enrichment.body: Walk every room at floor level this weekend: coins, batteries, magnets (neodymium sets are life-threatening if two are swallowed), small toy parts, pet food. Install outlet covers while you are down there - crawling typically starts at 7-10 months.

Prop him into supported sitting with toys in a semicircle and you as the backstop - 5-10-second tripod holds are the current working set. Offer a toy at midline and watch for the hand-to-hand transfer.
Restructure the day around three naps if the fourth is collapsing - wake windows run 2-2.5 hours at this age, and the last nap should end by 16:30-17:00 to protect an 18:30-19:30 bedtime.

Keep the weekly SFPL Baby Rhyme & Play Time slot on the standing calendar - free, ticketed at popular branches, and the Cantonese session doubles as live L2 exposure; the infant program runs to 15 months.

upcoming: Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - confirm it is booked. Bring the iron question if exclusively breastfed, the allergen plan, and sleep status.
Sat Sep 26, 2026 (week 20): the day 140-200 participatory-music enrollment window opens - decision brief next week.

subject: Week 20: participatory music class window opens - enroll one

content.hook: The one paid class with randomized-trial evidence behind it opens its window this week: active, participatory infant music. Enroll one - the participation is the ingredient, not the brand.
content.thisWeek: Days 138-144 approach the 6-month landmark: sitting with progressively less support, deliberate object examination (turn, mouth, transfer), and reduplicated babble (baba, dada - non-referential at this stage). Rolling is fluid for some; the CDC tummy-to-back checkpoint remains 6 months. His iron stores are beginning their pre-6-month depletion - solids will backfill via fortified cereal and iron-rich foods.
watchFors: [low concern] Mini sleep disruptions at developmental leaps even with the 4-month regression behind you - hold the routine steady rather than re-engineering it.
[low concern] Dada with no referent - reduplicated babble is a language milestone, not a first word; referential use comes months later.
[monitor] Persistent failure to roll, sit with support, or transfer objects hand to hand - flag for the 6-month visit.
[call within 24h] Acute illness onset or persistent feeding difficulties - same-day call.
[call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

enrichment.body: Enroll one weekly participatory music class. The Gerry/Unrau/Trainor 2012 randomized trial found active classes at 6 months beat passive listening on pitch and rhythm discrimination and prelinguistic gestures. Music Together SF runs rolling 10-week babies sessions ($405, or $380 on auto-enroll; enroll about two weeks before a session start); SFCM Smart Start's fixed August registration has passed for this fall, so Music Together is the live option. One class is the right dose - no dose-response evidence exists under 12 months.

Start Suzuki listening if early instrumental training is the plan: settle the instrument (violin and piano are the common calls), order the Book 1-2 repertoire recordings, and run them 30+ minutes a day during play or feeds. Years of listening precede lessons at age 3-4; the cost of the option now is recordings only.
Rotate in hand-eye coordination toys: stacking rings (target the ring toward the post) and a shape-sorter used for open exploration - sorting itself is not the goal yet.
Shift read-alouds toward dialogue: ask what's-that and pause for a response even though he is pre-verbal - the turn-taking, not the answer, is the input.

subject: Week 21: decide puree vs baby-led weaning before solids start

content.hook: First solids are roughly a month out, and the method decision - purees, baby-led weaning, or combo - is this week's call. The honest evidence summary: method matters less than allergen timing.
content.thisWeek: Days 145-151 are pre-6-month consolidation: supported sitting is steadier, with brief independent moments for some - the CDC sits-without-support checkpoint is 9 months, so support is still the norm. Rolling is now navigation, babble turn-taking sustains several exchanges, and he anticipates outcomes, smiling when the bath starts running. One epidemiological note: ear-infection incidence starts climbing from 6 months, usually riding on viral colds.
watchFors: [low concern] Drool surge ahead of the first tooth - eruption typically lands at 6-10 months.
[monitor] Ear-tugging without other illness signs - usually self-soothing or teething, occasionally early ear pain; watch for the fever pairing.
[call within 24h] Ear-tugging plus fever plus fussiness - possible otitis media; peak incidence runs 6-24 months.
[call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, persistent vomiting with reduced wet diapers, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

enrichment.body: Decide the solids method and stage the gear. Combo approaches are common and not harmful, and baby-led weaning does not increase choking risk versus purees in the randomized data - allergen timing matters more than method. Equipment: high chair, bibs, pre-loaded spoons, suction bowl, 2-oz silicone freezer cups, mat under the chair. First 5 foods: avocado, banana, sweet potato, iron-fortified oatmeal, well-cooked egg yolk - then peanut within the first two weeks of solids.
Log 30+ minutes outside daily - grass and sand under his hands, birdsong, traffic, wind, and light variation are the sensory curriculum at this age, free of charge.
Introduce cause-and-effect toys - a ball that rolls when pushed, a button that triggers music. This is the front edge of intentional action-outcome learning.
Use the final free-tier weeks at La Petite Baleen (933 Mason St) - the free infant-swim window ends when paid tuition starts at 6 months, around day 180.
Bank skipped or short naps into an earlier bedtime - 30-60 minutes forward - rather than a late-afternoon make-up nap that pushes the whole night later.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep

subject: Week 22: build the 6-month visit list - iron screen is universal

content.hook: The 6-month visit window opens in about two weeks. This week's job is the prep list - allergen plan review, the universal iron check, lead questionnaire, solids strategy, sleep status - so the appointment converts decisions instead of opening them.
content.thisWeek: Days 152-158 widen the social world: he knows familiar people, studies himself in the mirror, blows raspberries, and takes turns making sounds - a CDC 6-month checkpoint. Tripod sitting is emerging for some; the CDC sits-without-support checkpoint is 9 months, so propped is still the expected posture. His sharpening preference for the two of you is the precursor to stranger anxiety, which peaks at 7-10 months.
watchFors: [low concern] Increased clinginess and protest at being put down - attachment sharpening, on schedule.
[monitor] Little interest in toys, minimal vocalizing, or scarce eye contact - document and raise at the 6-month visit.
[monitor] Night wakings still at 4+ after six or more weeks of consistent response - see the sleep re-evaluation below.
[call within 24h] New ear-pulling with fever, or illness symptoms persisting past 48 hours - same-day call.
[call now] Seizure-like activity, fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - call 911, don't second-guess.

enrichment.body: Stock the solids shelf: iron-fortified single-grain oat cereal (the standard starting point) plus the week-one produce - avocado, banana, sweet potato. If baby-led weaning won the method decision, skip spoons and plan soft strips; if purees, a NumNum-style pre-loaded spoon.
Point and name consistently during read-alouds - this is a cat; the cat is on the mat. Conversational turns, not raw word count, are what predict language outcomes in the neuroimaging data.
Get on the floor at his eye level after sitting him up - lie down beside him rather than looming above. Eye-level interaction raises the quality of vocal turn-taking.

Re-evaluate the sleep plan if you rode out the regression: past week 22 with 4+ nightly wakings, pick a formal method and commit for seven nights. Graduated extinction shows meaningful improvement by night 5-7, with no measurable harm to behavior or attachment at 5-year follow-up (Hiscock 2012).
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep

enrichment.body: Register with Stanford SVNDL this week if the baby-lab batch never happened - the 3-6-month eligibility ceiling closes around day 180, four weeks out.
